title: GPX Start and End Coordinates Extractor
description: Extract the first and last coordinates of a GPX track or route with GPX Start and End Coordinates — the endpoints, read locally. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, the worked park loop starts at 40.7681, −73.9719 and ends at 40.7681, −73.9630 — same latitude, 0.75 kilometres apart, a loop that was never quite closed.
quick_answer: GPX Start and End Coordinates extracts the first and last coordinate from a GPX track's or route's point sequence. Load the file locally and read the two endpoints — the pair that identifies a route in any catalogue and frames its full extent.

Shuttle and pickup planning needs the finish coordinate exactly; the start coordinate is where the car goes. Both, copy-ready, from the file.
A loop's endpoints should nearly coincide. A 750-metre gap between start and finish means the recording started late, ended early, or the 'loop' is a line.

Start 40.7681, −73.9719; end 40.7681, −73.9630: identical latitude, longitude differing by 0.0089° — about 0.75 km of unfinished business, priced by the same degree arithmetic as the rest of this site.

A file with several tracks has several starts and ends. The extractor works from the point sequence you are asking about — first track by default order — because 'the start of the file' and 'the start of Saturday's leg' are different questions.
